# Tuya TS0044

![Tuya TS0044](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/assets/controllers/TS0044.jpeg>)

- **Manufacturer:** Tuya
- **Device ID:** `TS0044`
- **Controller types:** [Light](<#light>) (`TS0044LightController`)
- **Integrations:** [Zigbee2MQTT](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md>) (`z2m`)

[Build the configuration for this device](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/config-builder/index.md?device=TS0044>)

## Notes

Note that each button performs the same actions. This is because ControllerX is designed to control just one entity (light or media player). So, you can include the `actions` parameter to include the actions needed, or use the `mapping` attribute to define a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>). You can check [here](<https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/18#issuecomment-582535634>) for reference.

Also, this controller supports the hold action, but not release. This means that there are no smooth brightness changes when holding, just step by step every time it is held.

## Light

- **Class:** `TS0044LightController`
- **Entity parameter:** `light`
- **Default delay:** `350ms`

### Default mapping

Each row shows the events fired by the device for each integration and the [predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) they trigger by default. You can change it with a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>).

| Zigbee2MQTT | [Predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) |
| --- | --- |
| `1_single`, `2_single`, `3_single`, `4_single` | `toggle` |
| `1_double`, `2_double`, `3_double`, `4_double` | `click_brightness_up` |
| `1_hold`, `2_hold`, `3_hold`, `4_hold` | `click_brightness_down` |

### Example configuration

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: TS0044LightController
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: TS0044LightController
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event
  controller: my_controller_action
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

# Tuya TS0044F

![Tuya TS0044F](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/assets/controllers/TS0044F.jpeg>)

- **Manufacturer:** Tuya
- **Device ID:** `TS0044F`
- **Controller types:** [Light](<#light>) (`TS0044FLightController`)
- **Integrations:** [Zigbee2MQTT](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md>) (`z2m`)

[Build the configuration for this device](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/config-builder/index.md?device=TS0044F>)

## Notes

This device is very similar to the TS0044 Tuya, except that it doesn't support hold actions or double clicks.

Note that each button performs the same actions. This is because ControllerX is designed to control just one entity (light or media player). So, you can include the `actions` parameter to include the actions needed, or use the `mapping` attribute to define a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>). You can check [here](<https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/18#issuecomment-582535634>) for reference.

Since this controller doesn't support the hold action, there are no smooth brightness changes, just step by step every time it is pressed.

## Light

- **Class:** `TS0044FLightController`
- **Entity parameter:** `light`
- **Default delay:** `350ms`

### Default mapping

Each row shows the events fired by the device for each integration and the [predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) they trigger by default. You can change it with a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>).

| Zigbee2MQTT | [Predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) |
| --- | --- |
| `"on"`, `"off"` | `toggle` |
| `brightness_step_up` | `click_brightness_up` |
| `brightness_step_down` | `click_brightness_down` |

### Example configuration

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: TS0044FLightController
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: TS0044FLightController
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event
  controller: my_controller_action
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

## Light

- **Class:** `TerncyPP01LightController`
- **Entity parameter:** `light`
- **Default delay:** `350ms`

### Default mapping

Each row shows the events fired by the device for each integration and the [predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) they trigger by default. You can change it with a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>).

| ZHA | [Predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) |
| --- | --- |
| `button_single` | `toggle` |
| `button_double` | `on_full_brightness` |
| `button_triple` | `on_min_brightness` |
| `button_quadruple` | `set_half_brightness` |
| `button_quintuple` | `set_half_color_temp` |

### Example configuration

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: TerncyPP01LightController
  integration: zha
  controller: 00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

| `button_1_double`, `button_2_double`, `button_4_double` | `on_full_brightness` |
| `button_1_triple`, `button_1_hold`, `button_1_release`, `button_2_triple`, `button_2_hold`, `button_2_release`, `button_3_triple`, `button_4_triple`, `button_5_triple`, `button_6_triple` | *No action* |

| `button_3_double` | `on_min_brightness` |

| `button_4_hold` | `hold_brightness_up` |

| `button_6_single` | `click_colortemp_up` |
| `button_6_double` | `on_full_color_temp` |
| `button_6_hold` | `hold_colortemp_up` |

# Aqara WXKG02LM

![Aqara WXKG02LM](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/assets/controllers/WXKG02LM.jpeg>)

- **Manufacturer:** Aqara
- **Device ID:** `WXKG02LM`
- **Controller types:** [Light](<#light>) (`WXKG02LMLightController`), [Zigbee2MQTT Light](<#zigbee2mqtt-light>) (`WXKG02LMZ2MLightController`), [Switch](<#switch>) (`WXKG02LMSwitchController`)
- **Integrations:** [Zigbee2MQTT](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md>) (`z2m`), [deCONZ](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/deconz/index.md>) (`deconz`), [ZHA](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zha/index.md>) (`zha`)

[Build the configuration for this device](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/config-builder/index.md?device=WXKG02LM>)

## Notes

Note that all actions related to both left and right do the same. This is because ControllerX is designed to control just one entity (light or media player). So, you can include the `actions` parameter to include the actions needed. You can check [here](<https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/18#issuecomment-582535634>) for reference.

Also, this controller supports the hold action, but not release. This means that there are no smooth brightness changes when holding, just step by step every time it is held.

## Light

- **Class:** `WXKG02LMLightController`
- **Entity parameter:** `light`
- **Default delay:** `350ms`

### Default mapping

Each row shows the events fired by the device for each integration and the [predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) they trigger by default. You can change it with a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>).

| Zigbee2MQTT | deCONZ | ZHA | [Predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `single_both`, `single_left`, `single_right` | `1002`, `2002`, `3002` | `both_single`, `left_single`, `right_single` | `toggle` |
| `double_both`, `double_left`, `double_right` | `1004`, `2004`, `3004` | `both_double`, `left_double`, `right_double` | `click_brightness_up` |
| `hold_both`, `hold_left`, `hold_right` | `1001`, `2001`, `3001` | `both_long press`, `left_long press`, `right_long press` | `click_brightness_down` |

### Example configuration

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: WXKG02LMLightController
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: WXKG02LMLightController
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event
  controller: my_controller_action
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: WXKG02LMLightController
  integration: deconz
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: WXKG02LMLightController
  integration: zha
  controller: 00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88
  light: light.my_entity_id
```

Each row shows the events fired by the device for each integration and the [predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) they trigger by default. You can change it with a [custom mapping](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>).

| ZHA | [Predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md#light>) |
| --- | --- |

# Advanced

*This page assumes you already know how the [`mapping` attribute](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>) works.*

An action type is a reduced version of the Home Assistant [script syntax](<https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/scripts>). It defines one action or a sequence of actions to execute when an event is fired. The available action types are [predefined actions](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md>), service calls, scene activation and delays.

```
...
mapping: # or merge_mapping
  ## Predefined actions
  # `toggle` is a light predefined action
  <event>:
    action: toggle

  # The previous action type can be reduced as:
  <event>: toggle

  ## Call services
  # Call any service the same way as it is done through `Developer Tools > Services` in HA
  <event>:
    service: script.my_script
    data:
      attr1: 42
      attr2: foo

  # `entity_id` can be passed directly like this or through `data`.
  # Additionally, if the service is within the same domain
  # (light, media_player, etc) as the main entity from the configuration,
  # and entity_id is not passed, then it will use the one from the configuration.
  # This is handy, so there is no need to repeat the same entity over and over again.
  # Priority order for entity_id:
  # - Inside data
  # - In the same level as "service"
  # - From the main config if the domain matches
  <event>:
    service: light.turn_on
    entity_id: light.my_light

  ## Scene activation
  # Activate any HA Scene
  <event>:
    scene: scene.my_scene

  ## Delay
  # `delay` is useful when defining a list of actions, and you want
  # an action to be triggered after some defined time.
  # The value of the attribute only accepts seconds.
  <event>:
    - on_min_brightness # predefined action
    - delay: 5 # wait 5 seconds
    - on_full_brightness # predefined action
```

*The `<event>` key is the event from your controller and integration.*

If an action is still executing (most likely because of a `delay`) and the same event gets fired again, the behaviour depends on the [`mode`](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/configuration/index.md#parameters>) parameter, which works like the [Home Assistant automation modes](<https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/modes>). By default (`mode: single`), the new execution is ignored and a warning is logged. Use `mode: restart` to cancel the running action and start a new one.

Actions are executed sequentially, so it is not recommended to use a list of `hold` predefined actions, since it will not result in the expected behaviour. This is because `hold` actions are blocking operations, and they do not finish until a `release` action is fired.

*This is supported since ControllerX v4.14.0*

ControllerX allows entity controllers (LightController, MediaPlayerController, CoverController, etc.) to work with grouped entities.

All that is needed is an entity with an `entity_id` attribute containing the list of entities controlled by the group. For example, we can use a group entity from the [Group integration](<https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/group/>), or from the [Light Group integration](<https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light.group/>). ControllerX reads the attributes from the main entity (the first one in the list), but runs the actions on the grouped entity.

Let's imagine we have a Light Group entity (`light.livingroom`):

```
light:
  - platform: group
    name: livingroom
    entities:
      - light.livingroom_1
      - light.livingroom_2
      - light.livingroom_3
```

Then, we could configure the following in the `apps.yaml` file:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E2002LightController
  controller: livingroom_controller
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  light: light.livingroom
```

`light.livingroom_1` will be the main light that ControllerX reads from, but `light.livingroom` will be the grouped entity that ControllerX performs the actions on.

For example, if `light.livingroom_1` does not support `brightness`, but `light.livingroom_2` and `light.livingroom_3` do, then the configuration will not work because ControllerX will not be able to read the `brightness` attribute from `light.livingroom_1`.

*This is supported since ControllerX v4.23.0*

Most of the integrations supported by ControllerX are defined for a specific use case (Zigbee2MQTT, deCONZ, ZHA), but there is also the [`State` integration](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/state/index.md>), a more generic integration that allows us to listen to any Home Assistant entity state and build a mapping from it. Since ControllerX v4.23.0, we can also use the [`Event` integration](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/event/index.md>), which allows us to define the event we want to listen to and how to build the actions from it.

Each event has its own payload that could look like:

```
{
  "device_ieee": "00:67:88:56:06:78:9b:3f",
  "device_name": "my_device",
  "command": "step",
  "args": { "direction": "up" }
}
```

Then, ControllerX needs to convert this JSON-like data into an action string, such as `action_step_up`, so we can build our mapping on it.

Following this use case, we can create our own ControllerX configuration with this custom event:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: LightController
  controller: my_device # The value of the `controller_key` attribute defined below
  light: light.my_light
  integration:
    name: event # Required
    event_type: my_custom_event
    controller_key: device_name
    action_template: "action_{command}_{args[direction]}"
  mapping:
    action_step_up: click_brightness_up
    action_step_down: click_brightness_down
```

Let's break down the configuration for the integration:

- `event_type`: This is the event we will be listening to. For example, ZHA uses `zha_event`.
- `controller_key`: This is the attribute of the event data that identifies the controller. Its value must match the `controller` parameter. Note that the following names cannot be used for this field: `name`, `event`, `callback`, `namespace` or `cb`.
- `action_template`: This is the template used to build the name of the actions. We can use `{}` to retrieve the keys from the data, and `[]` inside them to access nested attributes, as shown in the example.

*This page assumes you already know how the [`mapping` attribute](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>) and [predefined actions](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md>) work.*

Since ControllerX v4.16.0, the hold and click actions can be configured. Before that, there were only the `{hold,click}_{brightness,color_temp,white_color,...}_{up,down,toggle}` predefined actions like:

- `hold_brightness_toggle`
- `hold_color_up`
- `click_colortemp_up`
- `click_brightness_down`
- ...

They allow using click (1 step) or hold (smooth dim) with different attributes and directions. However, it became difficult to extend them with more functionality, so the `click` and `hold` actions can now be configured as follows:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  integration: deconz
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_light
  merge_mapping:
    2001:
      action: click # [click, hold] This is the predefined action.
      attribute: brightness # [brightness, color_temp, white_value, color, xy_color]
      direction: up # [up, down, toggle (only for hold)]
      mode: stop # [stop, loop, bounce (only for hold)] Stepper mode
      steps: 10 # It overrides the `manual_steps` and `automatic_steps` global attributes
```

The fields are the following:

- **action**: This is the [predefined action](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/predefined-actions/index.md>), which in this case is `click` or `hold`.
- **attribute**: Attribute we want to act on. The available values are: `brightness`, `color_temp`, `white_value`, `color`, and `xy_color`. However, `xy_color` will ignore the `mode` and `steps` attributes since it already loops through the color wheel.
- **direction**: Direction to start. Options are `up`, `down`, and `toggle`. The `click` action does not accept `toggle`.
- **`up`**: It goes up.
- **`down`**: It goes down.
- **`toggle`**: It changes direction every time the action is performed.
- **mode**: This is the stepper mode. Options are `stop`, `loop`, and `bounce`. The `click` action does not accept `bounce`.
- **`stop`**: This is the default behaviour. It stops when it reaches either end (min or max).
- **`loop`**: It loops through all the values under the same direction, so when reaching the end, it will start over. For example, if you configure the brightness with direction `up`, it will go from the current value up to 255 (default max), and then it will start over from 1 (default min) without releasing the button. This `mode` will not stop unless there is a `release` action or it reaches the `max_loops` attribute (default is 50 steps).
- **`bounce`**: It bounces at the ends, so when reaching an end it switches direction. For example, if you configure the brightness with direction `down`, it will go from the current value down to 1 (default min), then it will start going up until reaching 255, and then bounce back again. This `mode` will not stop unless there is a `release` action or it reaches the `max_loops` attribute (default is 50 steps).

As you can see, the configuration is much more flexible, but it needs more lines than the direct predefined actions. For this reason, the predefined actions like `{hold,click}_{brightness,color_temp,white_color,...}_{up,down,toggle}` will not be removed, but no new ones will be added, since they can now be configured this way. For example, this configuration:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  integration: deconz
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_light
  merge_mapping:
    2001:
      action: hold
      attribute: brightness
      direction: up
```

is the same as:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  integration: deconz
  controller: my_controller
  light: light.my_light
  merge_mapping:
    2001:
      action: hold_brightness_up
```

The old predefined actions have `stop` as a default mode.

We can use the `mapping` attribute to completely override the default behaviour of a controller, or `merge_mapping` to override just the specified events and keep the rest of the default mapping. Both work the same way:

- **key**: The event fired by the controller. You can check these events in the page of each device in [supported controllers](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/controllers/index.md>). Note that they change depending on the controller and the integration (z2m, deconz, zha). The [multiple clicks functionality](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/multiple-clicks/index.md>) can be configured in the `key` part.
- **value**: An [action type](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/action-types/index.md>) or a list of them. These are the actions executed when the event (`key`) is fired.

Let's see an example:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1743Controller
  controller: livingroom_controller
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  light: light.livingroom
  merge_mapping:
    "off":
      - scene: scene.night
      - service: notify.telegram
        data:
          message: '"off" clicked'
```

In this example, the `key` is `"off"` (extracted from the Zigbee2MQTT mapping of the [E1743 IKEA controller](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/controllers/E1743/index.md#light>)) and the value is a list of 2 action types: one to activate a scene and the other to send a message through a HA service call.

*This page assumes you already know how the [`mapping` attribute](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>) works.*

Some controllers fire events for double, triple (or even quadruple) clicks, but others only fire single click events. This feature allows you to manage multiple clicks virtually, especially for those single click events.

When adding a new custom mapping for your controller, you can use a token (`$`) to indicate how many times an event needs to occur for the action to be fired. Let's see an example:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  controller: my_controller
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  light: light.my_light
  multiple_click_delay: 500 # default
  mapping:
    brightness_up_click: "on"
    toggle: click_color_down
    toggle$1: click_color_up
    toggle$2: "off"
```

This might be a silly example, but it is enough to highlight some points about this feature. In this configuration we see 2 actions: `brightness_up_click` (not "multi-clickable") and `toggle` ("multi-clickable"). We also see an attribute called `multiple_click_delay`, which indicates the delay (in milliseconds, 500 by default) before a multiple click action is triggered. Let's go over the following scenarios:

- `brightness_up_click` is clicked once: The `on` action will be triggered immediately, with no delay.
- `toggle` is clicked once: The `click_color_up` action will be triggered after 500ms. Also note that `toggle` and `toggle$1` are basically the same, so if both are present, the one with the token (`$`) prevails. So `click_color_down` will never be called.
- `toggle` is clicked twice (with less than 500ms between clicks): The `off` action will be triggered 500ms after the second click.

The next example shows a real use of this feature with the E1810 controller from IKEA.

```
livingroom:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  controller: livingroom_controller
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  light: light.livingroom_lamp
  smooth_power_on: true
  merge_mapping:
    toggle$2:
      service: light.toggle
      data:
        entity_id: light.livingroom_fairylights
    toggle$3:
      service: light.toggle
      data:
        entity_id: light.bedroom
```

This will keep the default mapping for the E1810 controller by using `merge_mapping` and add new actions when clicking the middle button 2 and 3 times, to toggle the fairy lights and the bedroom lamp.

Note that ControllerX registers the multiple-click events in the initialization phase by checking the events with `$`, so it records whether it needs to wait to trigger the multiple-click event or not. If the triggered event is not registered as multiple-clickable, then it will be triggered immediately. However, if the triggered event is multiple-clickable, then it will wait as long as specified in `multiple_click_delay` to detect whether another click is issued or not. If no second (n-th) click is registered, then the event is triggered. Therefore, all multi-clickable events will have a delay specified by `multiple_click_delay`.

*This page assumes you already know how the [`mapping` attribute](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/index.md>) works.*

Here you can find a list of predefined actions (one of the [action types](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/action-types/index.md>)) for each type of controller.

## Light

When using a [light controller](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/type-configuration/index.md#light-controller>) (e.g. `E1743Controller`) or `LightController`, the following actions can be used as a predefined action:

| value | description | parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"on"` | It turns on the light | \- `attributes`: a mapping with attribute and value |
| `"off"` | It turns off the light |  |
| `toggle` | It toggles the light | \- `attributes`: a mapping with attribute and value |
| `toggle_full_brightness` | It toggles the light, setting the brightness to the maximum value when turning on. |  |
| `toggle_full_white_value` | It toggles the light, setting the white value to the maximum value when turning on. |  |
| `toggle_full_color_temp` | It toggles the light, setting the color temperature to the maximum value when turning on. |  |
| `toggle_min_brightness` | It toggles the light, setting the brightness to the minimum value when turning on. |  |
| `toggle_min_white_value` | It toggles the light, setting the white value to the minimum value when turning on. |  |
| `toggle_min_color_temp` | It toggles the light, setting the color temperature to the minimum value when turning on. |  |
| `release` | It stops `hold` actions |  |
| `on_full_brightness` | It sets the brightness to the maximum value |  |
| `on_full_white_value` | It sets the white value to the maximum value |  |
| `on_full_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to the maximum value |  |
| `on_min_brightness` | It sets the brightness to the minimum value |  |
| `on_min_white_value` | It sets the white value to the minimum value |  |
| `on_min_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to the minimum value |  |
| `on_min_max_brightness` | It sets the brightness to the minimum value if the light is off or the brightness is different from the minimum value; otherwise, it sets the brightness to the maximum value. |  |
| `on_max_min_brightness` | It sets the brightness to the maximum value if the light is off or the brightness is different from the maximum value; otherwise, it sets the brightness to the minimum value. |  |
| `on_min_max_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to the minimum value if the light is off or the color temp is different from the minimum value; otherwise, it sets the color temp to the maximum value. |  |
| `on_max_min_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to the maximum value if the light is off or the color temp is different from the maximum value; otherwise, it sets the color temp to the minimum value. |  |
| `set_half_brightness` | It sets the brightness to 50% |  |
| `set_half_white_value` | It sets the white value to 50% |  |
| `set_half_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to 50% |  |
| `sync` | It syncs the light(s) to full brightness and white color or 2700K (370 mireds) | \- `brightness`<br>\- `color_temp`<br>\- `xy_color` |
| `click` | It increases/decreases the attribute according to the `manual_steps` attribute, and allows passing parameters through the YAML config. You can read more about it [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/hold-click-modes/index.md>). | \- `attribute`<br>\- `direction`<br>\- `mode`<br>\- `steps` |
| `click_brightness_up` | It increases the brightness according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_brightness_down` | It decreases the brightness according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_white_value_up` | It turns the white value up according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_white_value_down` | It turns the white value down according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_color_up` | It turns the color up according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_color_down` | It turns the color down according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_colortemp_up` | It turns the color temp up according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_colortemp_down` | It turns the color temp down according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_xycolor_up` | It turns the xy color up according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `click_xycolor_down` | It turns the xy color down according to the `manual_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold` | It increases/decreases the attribute until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute, and allows passing parameters through the YAML config. You can read more about it [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/hold-click-modes/index.md>). | \- `attribute`<br>\- `direction`<br>\- `mode`<br>\- `steps` |
| `hold_brightness_up` | It increases the brightness until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_brightness_down` | It decreases the brightness until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_brightness_toggle` | It increases/decreases the attribute until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute and alternates the direction on each click |  |
| `hold_white_value_up` | It turns the white value up until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_white_value_down` | It turns the white value down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_white_value_toggle` | It turns the white value up/down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute and alternates the direction on each click |  |
| `hold_color_up` | It turns the color up until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_color_down` | It turns the color down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_color_toggle` | It turns the color up/down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute and alternates the direction on each click |  |
| `hold_colortemp_up` | It turns the color temp up until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_colortemp_down` | It turns the color temp down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_colortemp_toggle` | It turns the color temp up/down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute and alternates the direction on each click |  |
| `hold_xycolor_up` | It turns the xy color up until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_xycolor_down` | It turns the xy color down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute |  |
| `hold_xycolor_toggle` | It turns the xy color up/down until release according to the `automatic_steps` attribute and alternates the direction on each click |  |
| `xycolor_from_controller` | It changes the xy color of the light from the value sent by the controller (if supported) |  |
| `colortemp_from_controller` | It changes the color temperature of the light from the value sent by the controller (if supported) |  |
| `brightness_from_controller_level` | It changes the brightness of the light from the value sent by the controller `action_level` (if supported) |  |
| `brightness_from_controller_angle` | It changes the brightness of the light from the value sent by the controller `action_rotation_angle` (if supported). This fires a `hold` action, so a `release` action is needed to stop the brightness change. | \- `mode`<br>\- `steps` |
| `brightness_from_controller_step` | It changes the brightness of the light from the value sent by the controller `step_mode`/`step_size` (if supported). |  |
| `colortemp_from_controller_step` | It changes the color temperature of the light from the value sent by the controller `step_mode`/`step_size` (if supported). |  |

| value | description | parameters |

| `toggle` | It toggles the light |  |
| `release` | It stops `hold` actions |  |
| `on_full_brightness` | It sets the brightness to the maximum value |  |
| `on_full_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to the maximum value |  |
| `on_min_brightness` | It sets the brightness to the minimum value |  |
| `on_min_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to the minimum value |  |
| `set_half_brightness` | It sets the brightness to 50% |  |
| `set_half_color_temp` | It sets the color temp to 50% |  |
