# Optional

If we want to use the `mqtt` or `tasmota` integrations, `listen_to: mqtt` in the `z2m` integration, or the `Z2MLightController` with `mode: mqtt`, we need to enable the AppDaemon MQTT plugin. How to do it depends on how you [installed ControllerX](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/installation/index.md>).

## ControllerX app

1. Go to **Settings → Apps → ControllerX → Configuration**.
2. Turn on **Enable MQTT**.
3. If you use the Mosquitto broker app, that's all: the app gets the broker address and credentials from Home Assistant. Otherwise, fill in **MQTT host** (without the port, e.g. `192.168.1.10`), **MQTT port**, **MQTT username** and **MQTT password**. They are under **Show unused optional configuration options**.
4. Save. Home Assistant offers to restart the app.

The app manages the AppDaemon configuration itself, so there's no `appdaemon.yaml` to edit.

## AppDaemon app

Add the following highlighted section to the AppDaemon configuration (`/app_configs/a0d7b954_appdaemon/appdaemon.yaml`):

```
---
appdaemon:
  latitude: X.XXXXXXX
  longitude: X.XXXXXXX
  elevation: XXXX
  time_zone: XXXXXXXX
  missing_app_warnings: 0 # (1)
  plugins:
    HASS:
      type: hass
      token: !env_var SUPERVISOR_TOKEN
    MQTT:
      type: mqtt
      namespace: mqtt # This is important
      client_id: appdaemon # (2)
      client_host: core-mosquitto # (3)
      client_user: XXXXX # (4)
      client_password: !secret mqtt_password # (5)
      client_topics: NONE # (6)
http:
  url: http://0.0.0.0:5050
admin:
api:
```

1. Extra tip: you can add `missing_app_warnings` if you don't want any warning spam from ControllerX when starting AppDaemon.
2. A name no other MQTT client uses. Without it, AppDaemon connects as `appdaemon_mqtt_client`, so if two AppDaemon instances use the same broker, the broker keeps disconnecting one of them.
3. `core-mosquitto` if you use the Mosquitto broker app. Otherwise, the host of your MQTT broker without the port (e.g. 192.168.1.10).
4. The user and password of your MQTT broker.
5. Add `mqtt_password: <your password>` to `secrets.yaml`, next to `appdaemon.yaml` (or to the file set in `secrets:`, if your `appdaemon.yaml` has that line). You can also write the password here directly.
6. Optional. By default, AppDaemon subscribes to every MQTT topic (`#`) and receives every message in the broker, even though ControllerX only needs the topics of your controllers. With `NONE`, ControllerX subscribes to just those topics. Leave it out if other AppDaemon apps of yours listen to MQTT topics without subscribing to them.

Then restart the AppDaemon app.

[AppDaemon](<https://appdaemon.readthedocs.io/>) lets you write Home Assistant automations in Python instead of YAML. For simple automations, YAML or the automation editor are great, but when automations get more complicated, they become difficult to manage in YAML. This is where AppDaemon comes in.

This is the reason this project is built on top of AppDaemon. Now you might be convinced, but have no idea how to install and set it up. If you are using Home Assistant OS, the [installation](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/installation/index.md>) page explains your options: the ControllerX app, which includes its own AppDaemon, or the `AppDaemon` app from the app store with ControllerX installed in it, either through AppDaemon Store or manually.

How to update ControllerX depends on how you [installed it](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/installation/index.md>):

- **ControllerX app:** update the app from **Settings → Apps**. The app restarts on its own.
- **AppDaemon Store:** update ControllerX from the AppDaemon Store UI (or enable auto-update). AppDaemon Store restarts the AppDaemon app on its own (see [AppDaemon Store and AppDaemon app](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/installation/index.md#appdaemon-store-and-appdaemon-app>)).
- **Manual installation:** replace the `controllerx` folder with the latest release and restart the AppDaemon app (see [Manual installation](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/installation/index.md#manual-installation>)).

With a manual installation, remember to restart AppDaemon after installing a new version of ControllerX, since AppDaemon does not reimport the modules. If AppDaemon is not restarted, it will keep running the old version.

*Zigbee2MQTT HA sensor deprecated since ControllerX v4.29.0*

Zigbee2MQTT 2.0.0 brought [some breaking changes](<https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt/discussions/24198>), and one of them was to deprecate the [Home Assistant action sensors](<https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/usage/integrations/home_assistant.html#via-home-assistant-action-sensor-deprecated>), which is the default option of the [Zigbee2MQTT integration](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md>) in ControllerX.

You might be here because of a warning in the AppDaemon logs that looks like the following:

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Quote**
>
> ⚠️ Listening to HA sensor actions is now deprecated and will be removed in the future. Use `listen_to: mqtt` or `listen_to: event` instead. Read more about it here: https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/others/z2m-ha-sensor-deprecated

This might be because your controller configuration looks like:

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  controller: sensor.livingroom_controller_action
  integration: z2m
  light: light.livingroom
```

The issue is `integration: z2m`, which reads a HA `sensor` by default. You need to switch to either [`mqtt`](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md#mqtt-topics-listen_to-mqtt>) (recommended) or HA [`event`](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md#event-state-listen_to-event>) (experimental).

## Switch to MQTT listener (recommended)

To switch to MQTT (as [recommended by Zigbee2MQTT](<https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/usage/integrations/home_assistant.html#via-mqtt-device-trigger-recommended>)), you first need to [enable the MQTT plugin](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/others/enable-mqtt-plugin/index.md>). Then, change your configuration to something like the following:

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  controller: livingroom_controller # (1)
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt # (2)
  light: light.livingroom
```

1. This is the friendly name of the device in Zigbee2MQTT. Check [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md#mqtt-topics-listen_to-mqtt>) how to get this value.
2. With `mqtt`, ControllerX listens to the MQTT topic of the controller.

## Switch to HA Event sensor listener (experimental)

Another option is to listen to the new (and experimental) event entity from Zigbee2MQTT 2.0.0. First, enable the experimental feature in Zigbee2MQTT as explained [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md#event-state-listen_to-event>). Then, change your configuration to something like:

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller
  controller: livingroom_controller_action # (1)
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event # (2)
  light: light.livingroom
```

1. This is the event entity without the `event.` prefix. Check [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md#event-state-listen_to-event>) how to get this value.
2. With `event`, ControllerX listens to the changes of the event entity.

*This is supported since ControllerX v4.21.0*

ControllerX has always supported the [Light Controller](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/type-configuration/index.md#light-controller>), which, amongst other features, smoothly changes attributes (brightness, color temperature) by periodically requesting the changes to Home Assistant. This works with lights from many integrations (e.g. Zigbee2MQTT, deCONZ, WLED, Hue). However, this generalization penalizes Zigbee2MQTT, which has its own mechanism to change the brightness and color temperature over time, and works much more smoothly than the Light Controller.

Zigbee2MQTT allows sending a payload like `{"brightness_move": -40}` to the `zigbee2mqtt/FRIENDLY_NAME/set` topic, which decreases the brightness 40 steps per second over time. Then, we can send the following payload to the same topic to make it stop: `{"brightness_move": "stop"}`. Zigbee2MQTT does not have a specific page documenting this, since it depends on the device. For example, we can see all this further explained for the [LED1545G12](<https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/devices/LED1545G12.html#light>) light.

Ideally, this would be part of the Light Controller, but there are many features that are not compatible with what Zigbee2MQTT offers:

- [Hold/Click modes](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/hold-click-modes/index.md>) (bounce, loop)
- Color looping
- Minimum and maximum attribute values

For this reason, there is a separate controller type, [Z2M Light Controller](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/type-configuration/index.md#zigbee2mqtt-light-controller>), which offers most of the functionality of the Light Controller, but uses the MQTT features from Zigbee2MQTT.

Imagine we have a light with the friendly name `livingroom` in Zigbee2MQTT and the entity `light.livingroom` in Home Assistant. Then, let's say we had the following ControllerX configuration for [E1810](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/controllers/E1810/index.md>):

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Controller # (1)
  controller: livingroom_controller_action
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event
  light: light.livingroom
```

1. `E1810Controller` is a `Light Controller`

This allows us to control the `livingroom` light with the Light Controller. However, if we replace `E1810Controller` with `E1810Z2MLightController`, and `light.livingroom` with `livingroom`, we will be using the Z2M Light Controller:

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Z2MLightController # (1)
  controller: livingroom_controller_action
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event
  light: livingroom # (2)
```

1. This is a `Z2M Light Controller`
2. This is the Zigbee2MQTT friendly name of the light

This sends the MQTT messages through Home Assistant, but if we have the [MQTT plugin enabled](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/others/enable-mqtt-plugin/index.md>) in AppDaemon, we can send them through the MQTT plugin instead:

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Z2MLightController
  controller: livingroom_controller_action
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: event
  light:
    name: livingroom
    mode: mqtt # (1)
```

1. `mode` can either be `ha` or `mqtt` (default: `ha`). On the one hand, `ha` sends the MQTT messages through Home Assistant with the [`mqtt.publish` service](<https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/mqtt/service/#service-mqttpublish>). On the other hand, `mqtt` sends the MQTT messages through the AppDaemon MQTT plugin (hence skipping HA).

Finally, we can have ControllerX both listening and sending to the MQTT broker directly, without going through Home Assistant:

```
livingroom_controller:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1810Z2MLightController
  controller: livingroom_controller # (1)
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  light:
    name: livingroom
    mode: mqtt
```

1. `livingroom_controller` is the Zigbee2MQTT friendly name of the controller

With this configuration, we can keep using the light even if Home Assistant is down, since all the interactions go:

```
Zigbee2MQTT <> MQTT Broker <> AppDaemon (ControllerX)
```

Many of the supported devices have a Zigbee2MQTT light controller class, which can be used in `class` the same way as their light controller class. Check the [supported controllers](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/controllers/index.md>) pages to see the class names.

#### 1\. I placed the configuration in configuration.yaml and it doesn't work

ControllerX depends on AppDaemon, and all the configuration for AppDaemon apps goes into `apps.yaml` in the AppDaemon apps folder (see [Installation](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/installation/index.md>)) and not `/config/configuration.yaml`.

#### 2\. I updated ControllerX to a new version and it does not work

If you installed ControllerX manually, the AppDaemon app (or server) needs to be restarted after updating ControllerX. AppDaemon Store restarts the AppDaemon app on its own after an update. The ControllerX app restarts on its own when updated.

#### 3\. I properly configured E1744 (symfonisk) with z2m but it doesn't work

The Zigbee2MQTT documentation recommends setting the `debounce` attribute. However, when it is set, the controller does not send an empty state, and its state stays active instead of being removed. This causes problems for ControllerX, so if you want to use this controller, I recommend removing the `debounce` attribute, since ControllerX already handles repeated events by itself.

#### 4\. I have a group of lights and it does not work properly

Please read [entity groups](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/advanced/entity-groups/index.md>) to understand how grouped entities work.

#### 5\. Error: "Value for X attribute could not be retrieved from light Y"

This error is shown when the light supports the X attribute (e.g. brightness or color\_temp), but the attribute is not in the state attributes of the entity. You can check whether the attribute X is shown in the state attributes in "Developer Tools \> States".

#### 6\. Light is not turning on to the previous brightness

Zigbee does not support transitions natively for lights, so this depends on the integration you use for your light. By default, ControllerX adds a transition when changing the brightness or color, but not when turning the light on/off. So if this is happening to you, it might be because `add_transition_turn_toggle: true` is set in your controller configuration. These are the issues related to this problem in the different integrations:

- [Zigbee2MQTT](<https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee-herdsman-converters/issues/1073>) (FIXED)
- [Hue integration](<https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/32894>) (CLOSED, but not fixed)

#### 7\. When holding or rotating the controller (especially the Symfonisk - E1744), it doesn't stop changing the brightness or volume

This is a known issue that cannot be fixed in the code. Controllers with hold-release functionality fire 2 events: one when the holding/rotation starts and another one when it stops rotating or is released. In between, ControllerX periodically calls HA services to update your brightness, volume, etc. (see [how it works](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/index.md#how-it-works>)).

If this happens to you sometimes, it is because the stop/release action has not been received. This can happen because:

- The rotation is too fast, so the controller cannot tell whether it stopped or not.
- The network is overloaded.
- The server cannot handle the requests on time.
- The controller and the light are far away from the coordinator.

However, these are some things you can do to reduce how often this happens:

- If the `release` action is sent at almost the same time as the `hold` one, you can use the [`release_delay` attribute](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/type-configuration/index.md#light-controller>) to delay `release` actions by some time after they are fired. For example: `release_delay: 0.01` (time in seconds).
- If using z2m, change the integration to listen to MQTT directly, so it avoids the HA state machine layer. Read more about it [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/index.md>).
- If using deCONZ and you just want to dim your lights smoothly, then you can consider using [this AppDaemon app](<https://github.com/Burningstone91/Hue_Dimmer_Deconz>) from [*@Burningstone91*](<https://github.com/Burningstone91>). It brightens/dims your lights with deCONZ calls instead of calling HA periodically, which means that deCONZ handles the dimming for you.
- Play around with the `delay` (default is 350ms) and `automatic_steps` (default is 10) attributes. You can read more about them [here](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/start/type-configuration/index.md#light-controller>). The lower the delay, the more requests are sent to HA. The higher `automatic_steps`, the more steps it takes to get from min to max, and vice versa.
- Add more Zigbee routers to the network.

#### 8\. Symfonisk controller (E1744) is not working with Zigbee2MQTT integration

Do you have a configuration that seems to be right, but is not working? The default mapping for E1744 uses the actions of the new (non-legacy) Zigbee2MQTT implementation for this controller, so you will need to [deactivate the legacy mode](<https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/devices/E1744.html#legacy-integration>) for this controller in Zigbee2MQTT. If you use the Zigbee2MQTT app, the device-specific configuration is in `/share/zigbee2mqtt/devices.yaml`. Add `legacy: false` to your E1744 controller as shown in the Zigbee2MQTT documentation, and restart Zigbee2MQTT. While you are here, I strongly recommend checking [FAQ \#9](<#9-symfonisk-controller-e1744-works-but-pretty-laggy>) if your controller feels slow.

#### 9\. Symfonisk controller (E1744) works, but pretty laggy

If you are using the `sensor` entity as your controller, I recommend changing the configuration to listen to MQTT directly instead of HA. For this, you will need to change your controller configuration (`apps.yaml`) and enable the AppDaemon MQTT plugin. Your new controller configuration will look like this:

```
example_app:
  module: controllerx
  class: E1744MediaPlayerController
  controller: my_z2m_friendly_name # This is the Zigbee2MQTT friendly name
  integration:
    name: z2m
    listen_to: mqtt
  media_player: media_player.my_media_player
```

Notice how we added the `listen_to` attribute and changed the `controller` to the Zigbee2MQTT friendly name. Finally, you will also need to have the [MQTT plugin enabled](<https://xaviml.github.io/controllerx/others/enable-mqtt-plugin/index.md>).
